summary:
Worked all 9 session-management items on shop.lab.test (HTTP only) using the admin (carol) and user (alice) test sessions; read-only, no writes.

Findings:
- Schema (01): server-side session carried in one cookie "lab_session"; distinct per-user values; 401 without it; cleared on logout.
- Cookie attributes (02): "lab_session=...; Path=/; Max-Age=31536000" with NO Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite, on a HTTP-only site — confirms the recon high lead. Same for both roles.
- Fixation (03): no pre-auth cookie issued by /login; forged value rejected (401); logout invalidates. Post-login rotation not testable read-only (login POST needs writes).
- Exposed session vars (04): no session id in URLs/bodies, but authenticated /account/settings is returned with "Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600" (new medium lead). app.js also exposes a Stripe pk and an AWS key id (redacted at storage).
- CSRF (05): sign-in and change-password forms have no anti-CSRF token and cookie has no SameSite — forgeable (new medium lead); change-password also takes only new_password (ties to recon medium lead).
- Logout (06): GET /account/logout terminates session (Max-Age=0), but being GET it is CSRF-able.
- Timeout (07): 1-year persistent cookie, no short timeout evident; server-side idle expiry not measurable read-only.
- Puzzling (08): unknown/missing session both yield 401; each session resolves to its own identity; no cross-contamination seen.
- Hijacking (09): missing HttpOnly/Secure over HTTP makes the session id stealable; replay with a genuine stolen value not exercised read-only.

Left partially open by nature of read-only: post-login session rotation (03), precise server-side timeout (07), and live hijack replay (09) — all require login/write actions not permitted in this engagement. Recorded two new medium leads (public cache-control on authenticated pages; GET logout / missing CSRF tokens).
